text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000395 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation, and 99215 rates are elevated even among patients with zero or one chronic condition, but documentation is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The pattern is partly consistent with a sicker panel, since 99215 share rises steeply with condition count. Yet it runs above the all-provider share in every complexity band, and over a quarter of 99215s fall on low-complexity patients. Examples include C0230342, C0230479 and C0230617, each with no chronic conditions and only a Z09 follow-up code, and C0230285, coded for obesity alone. That part of the pattern is consistent with upcoding. Only one 99215 was documented (C0230316, supported at high MDM), and 2 of 8 documented 99214s fell below the billed level (C0230312, C0230610), so the records sample cannot support a leaning either way. The single note claiming moderate-plus data review with no lab or test line on the claim is weak evidence at most. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the zero-condition Z09 visits, to see whether the documented MDM or time supports the level billed."}
